Nvidia shares surged 31.5%, adding a record $952bn to its market capitalisation, while the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 gained 6.9% and 4.7% respectively. Huang is due to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on 3 December, with Democrats promising further investigations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the reports on Monday. ... The warnings come amid growing competition between Russia, China and the US to develop offensive capabilities in space. US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink confirmed in September that Washington had deployed a weapon in orbit, without disclosing its capabilities. items.title: AI boom looms over Warsh’s Fed as inflation worries grow By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has called artificial intelligence a "hinge" of history critical to US leadership, but the technology has also become key to Fed policy as officials debate whether the AI boom is a transformational moment, a source of inflation, or the harbinger of an economic meltdown. ... Recent inflation and growth data "is too hot and too strong ... But with growth dependent on AI investment and AI consumer net-worth effects, the Fed needs any weakening to remain contained," Guha wrote. "Warsh needs to balance the data with markets that suggest the forward look is cooler, and his desire to assert inflation credibility with his desire not to go down in history as the Fed chair who blew up the AI boom." After a run that saw a political backlash against AI, a market slump, a major initial public offering, a massive corporate scandal, and a seeming rebound from it all with equity markets again surging, Fed officials are expected to follow through with a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at their December 8-9 meeting. While they do not necessarily aim to — or have any guarantee they can — slow the AI boom, many see it pushing growth beyond potential and see the need to restrain some aspects of investment and demand. "If the investment rate slows way down, then yes, I’d be less concerned that there would be overheating in the economy," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told reporters last week, likening the strain AI puts on capacity to trying to get a "pig through the python." But the impact of rate hikes on the economy "doesn’t have to be sector by sector," he said. "The Fed has only one tool, which is to tighten rates ... I do think data centers are included in that business investment" and might be influenced by rising borrowing costs.

items.title: US Inflation Rises 0.4% as November 25 PCE Report Looms | Investing.com
items.excerpt: U.S. consumer prices increased 0.4% in October, leaving investors with another inflation test as the Federal Reserve approaches its December interest-rate decision. The October Consumer Price Index (CPI), released November 10, showed slower monthly price growth than September but continued pressure in several important categories. Attention now turns to the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report, scheduled for Wednesday, November 25, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. That release could provide a more complete picture of inflation before policymakers meet again. The official CPI report showed that headline consumer prices rose 0.4% after increasing 0.6% in September, a slowdown of 0.2 percentage points. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% for a third consecutive month. Shelter prices rose 0.3%, while food prices increased 0.5%, indicating that slower overall inflation did not mean prices were falling across major household expenses. For investors, the distinction between softer headline inflation and persistent underlying price pressure is important. The October report also contained an unusual limitation. The Bureau of Labor Statistics could not publish most year-over-year inflation comparisons because it lacked the corresponding October 2025 price indexes following a lapse in federal appropriations. That leaves investors without the usual annual headline and core CPI readings, even though the monthly figures remain available. ... CPI and PCE should not be treated as interchangeable indicators. They differ in their expenditure weights, coverage and calculation methods, meaning a 0.4% CPI increase does not automatically imply the same monthly movement in PCE inflation.
